text_blocks.snippet: Blood pressure of 130/80 mm Hg or higher is officially considered high blood pressure (hypertension).

Blood pressure is written as two numbers. The top number is systolic pressure, and the bottom number is diastolic pressure. According to guidelines from the American Heart Association, readings fall into specific categories:

list.snippet: Normal: Less than 120 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic.
Elevated: 120–129 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic.
Stage 1 Hypertension: 130–139 mm Hg systolic or 80–89 mm Hg diastolic.
Stage 2 Hypertension: 140 mm Hg or higher systolic or 90 mm Hg or higher diastolic.
Hypertensive Crisis: Higher than 180 mm Hg systolic and/or higher than 120 mm Hg diastolic. Readings this high require immediate medical help.

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more about official standards through the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention or the National Institutes of Health.
